filters.name: Reconstruct Surface by Ball Pivoting (Gruber)
filters.shortDescription: Reconstruct a surface from oriented points using a direct implementation of the original Ball Pivoting paper.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Rolls a ball of the given radius over the point cloud: starting from a seed triangle the ball pivots around each boundary edge until it lands on another point, which makes the next triangle, and so on until the front runs out. Every vertex of the result is one of the input points -- nothing is invented, nothing is moved.

This is Bernhard Gruber's implementation, a direct and deliberately unelaborated reading of the 1999 paper. MeshLab also ships **Reconstruct Surface by Ball Pivoting (vcglib)**, and the two behave very differently on the same cloud, which is why both are here:

| | this filter | (vcglib) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| seeds | one, and the front grows from it alone | re-seeds, so every disconnected piece is covered |
| radius | you give it | you give it, or 0 to guess from the bounding box |
| clustering | none -- every input point stands | merges points closer than a clustering radius |
| creases | none -- the ball rolls over any fold | stops at a crease angle you set |

The single seed is the difference you will notice first. On a cloud in several pieces this one reconstructs whichever piece its seed landed in and leaves the rest bare; that is the published algorithm, and the filter says so in its report when it happens. Against that, nothing is clustered away, so on a cloud you have already sampled evenly it gives you back exactly the points you put in.

Works best on uniformly sampled clouds. If the sampling is uneven, run **Sample Surface by Poisson Disk** first. The points must carry normals, and they must be oriented consistently -- the ball needs to know which side the surface is on.

Reference:
Bernardini F., Mittleman J., Rushmeier H., Silva C., Taubin G., **The ball-pivoting algorithm for surface reconstruction**, IEEE TVCG 1999.

parameters.label: Pivoting Ball Radius
parameters.help: Radius of the ball rolled over the points. Gaps wider than the ball are left open, and pits narrower than it are bridged over. There is no autoguess here, unlike the vcglib implementation: pick something close to the spacing of the cloud, and raise it until the holes close.

parameters.label: Delete Initial Set of Faces
parameters.help: Throw away any faces the layer already has and rebuild from the points alone. This implementation always starts from its own seed triangle and cannot grow a front from existing faces, so leaving this off simply keeps the old faces alongside the new ones.
